arxiv-2111-04285.title: Dineutron in the 2 1 + 2^{+}_{1} state of 6 He
arxiv-2111-04285.creator: Shoya Ogawa, Takuma Matsumoto
arxiv-2111-04285.description: Abstract We investigate the dineutron in the 2 1 + 2^{+}_{1} state of 6 He via analysis of its decay mode by using the complex scaling method. In this letter, we propose the cross section for the resonant state to distinguish the resonant contributions from the nonresonant ones.

arxiv-2410-20269.title: Machine Learning Based Glitch Veto for inspiral binary merger signals using Linear Chirp Transform
arxiv-2410-20269.creator: N.Arutkeerthi, Xiyuan Li, SR Valluri
arxiv-2410-20269.description: Abstract Unphysical templates for binary inspiral merger signals have emerged as an effective approach to veto signals ( rule out false signals ) identified as glitches. They offer a promising solution to reduce the number of parameters necessary for distinguishing glitches from actual gravitational wave merger signals.

arxiv-2501-05447.title: On the addition technique for Betti and Poincaré polynomials of plane curves
arxiv-2501-05447.creator: Piotr Pokora
arxiv-2501-05447.description: Abstract Using the addition technique, we present polynomial identities for the Betti and Poincaré polynomials of reduced plane curves. Keywords reduced curves, quasi-homogeneous singularities, conic-line arrangements Mathematics Subject Classification (2020) 14H50, 32S25, 14N10 1 Introduction In this paper we study Poincaré polynomials for plane curves with quasi-homogeneous singularities in the context of the addition technique.

arxiv-2508-19818.title: Towards a Real-Time Warning System for Detecting Inaccuracies in Photoplethysmography-Based Heart Rate Measurements in Wearable Devices CCS: Human-centered computing Human computer interaction (HCI) CCS: Human-centered computing Ubiquitous and mobile devices CCS: Applied computing Health informatics
arxiv-2508-19818.creator: Rania Islambouli, Marlene Brunner, Devender Kumar, Mahdi Sareban, Gunnar Treff, Michael Neudorfer, Josef Niebauer, Arne Bathke, Jan David Smeddinck
arxiv-2508-19818.description: Abstract . Wearable devices with photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors are widely used to monitor heart rate (HR), yet often suffer from accuracy issues. However, users typically do not receive an indication of potential measurement errors. We present a real-time warning system that detects and communicates inaccuracies in PPG-derived HR, aiming to enhance transparency and trust.

arxiv-2509-14504.title: Introducing OmniGEC: A Silver Multilingual Dataset for Grammatical Error Correction
arxiv-2509-14504.creator: Roman Kovalchuk, Mariana Romanyshyn, Petro Ivaniuk
arxiv-2509-14504.description: Abstract In this paper, we introduce OmniGEC, a collection of multilingual silver-standard datasets for the task of Grammatical Error Correction (GEC), covering eleven languages: Czech, English, Estonian, German, Greek, Icelandic, Italian, Latvian, Slovene, Swedish, and Ukrainian. These datasets facilitate the development of multilingual GEC solutions and help bridge the data gap in adapting English GEC solutions to multilingual GEC.

arxiv-2511-15830.title: Mini Amusement Parks (MAPs): A Testbed for Modelling Business Decisions
arxiv-2511-15830.creator: Stéphane Aroca-Ouellette, Ian Berlot-Attwell, Panagiotis Lymperopoulos, Abhiramon Rajasekharan, Tongqi Zhu, Herin Kang, Kaheer Suleman, Sam Pasupalak
arxiv-2511-15830.description: Abstract Despite rapid progress in artificial intelligence, current systems struggle with the interconnected challenges that define real-world decision making. Practical domains, such as business management, require optimizing an open-ended and multi-faceted objective, actively learning environment dynamics from sparse experience, planning over long horizons in stochastic settings, and reasoning over spatial information.

pmc-10507886.title: Triglyceride–glucose index and the risk of stroke in American adults: findings from the atherosclerosis risk in communities study
pmc-10507886.creator: Xinyi Wang, Qiyu Liu, Tongxin Wang, Wende Tian, Xuanye Chen, Jie Zhang, Qiuyi Li, Dan Ma, Lin Zhao, Zhuo Chen, Hao Xu, Keji Chen
pmc-10507886.description: ObjectivesThe associations between the triglyceride–glucose (TyG) index with subsequent stroke in American adults are unknown. The aim of this study was to determine the associations between baseline and trajectories of TyG index with subsequent stroke in American adults.MethodsA total of 10,132 participants free of a history of stroke at baseline were included.

pmc-10671503.title: Comparative Transcriptomic Analysis of Largemouth Bass (Micropterus salmoides) Livers Reveals Response Mechanisms to High Temperatures
pmc-10671503.creator: Fan Zhou, Ming Qi, Jiapeng Li, Yuanfei Huang, Xiaoming Chen, Wei Liu, Gaohua Yao, Qinghui Meng, Tianlun Zheng, Zhanqi Wang, Xueyan Ding, Manuel Vera Rodríguez
pmc-10671503.description: High temperatures are considered one of the most significant limitations to subtropical fishery production. Largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) is an economically important freshwater species grown in subtropical areas, which are extremely sensitive to heat stress (HS). However, comprehensive transcriptomic data for the livers of largemouth bass in response to HS are still lacking.

pmc-11401518.title: Cybervictimization and Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among Chinese College Students: an Exploration Through the Lens of Experiential Avoidance Model
pmc-11401518.creator: Ying Chen, Hanyu Liang, Huaibin Jiang
pmc-11401518.description: PurposeNon-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a growing public health concern among college students, with cybervictimization (CV) emerging as a significant contributing factor. Grounded in the experiential avoidance theory, this study investigates the mediating roles of cognitive fusion and negative emotions in the relationship between CV and NSSI, providing new insights into these key variables.

pmc-11435508.title: Detection Method for Three-Phase Electricity Theft Based on Multi-Dimensional Feature Extraction
pmc-11435508.creator: Wei Bai, Lan Xiong, Yubei Liao, Zhengyang Tan, Jingang Wang, Zhanlong Zhang
pmc-11435508.description: The advent of smart grids has facilitated data-driven methods for detecting electricity theft, with a preponderance of research efforts focused on user electricity consumption data. The multi-dimensional power state data captured by Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) encompasses rich information, the exploration of which, in relation to electricity usage behaviors, holds immense potential for enhancing the efficiency of theft detection.

pmc-11589328.title: Direct RNA sequencing in plants: Practical applications and future perspectives
pmc-11589328.creator: Xi-Tong Zhu, Pablo Sanz-Jimenez, Xiao-Tong Ning, Muhammad Tahir ul Qamar, Ling-Ling Chen
pmc-11589328.description: The transcriptome serves as a bridge that links genomic variation to phenotypic diversity. A vast number of studies using next-generation RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) over the last 2 decades have emphasized the essential roles of the plant transcriptome in response to developmental and environmental conditions, providing numerous insights into the dynamic changes, evolutionary traces, and elaborate regulation of the plant transcriptome.

pmc-11705623.title: Incidence of infective endocarditis in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
pmc-11705623.creator: Somyata Somendra, Saurabh Mehrotra, Parag Barwad, Himanshu Gupta, Ajay Bahl
pmc-11705623.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundData on the incidence of infective endocarditis (IE) in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is sparse. This study evaluated a HCM cohort with aim to study the incidence of IE in these patients.MethodsAll patients entering the HCM cohort from May 2003 to June 2022 of a tertiary care hospital with at least one follow-up visit were included and followed up till June 2023. This was a retrospective cohort analysis.

pmc-12528836.title: Stereoelectroencephalography Reveals Neural Signatures of Multisensory Integration in the Human Superior Temporal Sulcus during Audiovisual Speech Perception
pmc-12528836.creator: Yue Zhang, John F. Magnotti, Xiang Zhang, Zhengjia Wang, Yingjia Yu, Kathryn A. Davis, Sameer A. Sheth, H. Isaac Chen, Daniel Yoshor, Michael S. Beauchamp
pmc-12528836.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Human speech perception is multisensory, integrating auditory information from the talker's voice with visual information from the talker's face. BOLD fMRI studies have implicated the superior temporal gyrus (STG) in processing auditory speech and the superior temporal sulcus (STS) in integrating auditory and visual speech, but as an indirect hemodynamic measure, fMRI is limited in its ability to track the rapid neural computations underlying speech perception.

pmc-13009457.title: Targeting sialic acid metabolism: a therapeutic strategy against gastric cancer driven by WZ35
pmc-13009457.creator: Boxiang Hong, Ying Wang, Xinran Feng, Lihan Wei, Yichen Huang, Xiawei Zhang, Longyuchen Xu, Pinyan Jin, Liyuan Huang, Rui Li, Xinyu Wu, Zhi Li, Hangyu Ye, Tongke Chen, Xiaoyan Wang, Hao Zhang
pmc-13009457.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Glycolytic reprogramming is closely associated with the occurrence and progression of gastric cancer. Specifically, the energy derived from glucose metabolism and the cellular proteins by its intermediate products influence gastric cancer development. However, as an important branch of glucose metabolism, sialic acid metabolism and its mediated sialylation modifications remain insufficiently studied in gastric cancer, and their specific relationship with malignant tumor progression requires further exploration.

pmc-13096192.title: Modeling roles and trade-offs in multiplex networks
pmc-13096192.creator: Nikolaos Nakis, Sune Lehmann, Nicholas A. Christakis, Morten Mørup
pmc-13096192.description: Multiplex social networks capture multiple types of relations among the same people. Their structure reflects how exchanges arise from individual attributes related to independence, the status or resources of others related to dependence, and mutual influence related to interdependence. Understanding these systems is challenging because layers can play distinct yet complementary roles.

pmc-13166541.title: Coping strategies as modifiable pathways to posttraumatic growth in young adults facing parental cancer
pmc-13166541.creator: Erma Pratiwi Nufi, Alber Tigor Arifyanto, Minarti Usman, Wa Ode Lili Andriani Nasri, Ismail Ismail
pmc-13166541.description: This important work addresses a previously underrepresented demographic, offering valuable insights into the psychological processes that underpin resilience in the context of familial cancer. Among the study’s many strengths, its identification of coping strategies as significant mediators in the pathway from illness perception to PTG stands out as particularly actionable (Leis et al. 2024).

pmc-13374526.title: Implementing calculated globulin screening for immunodeficiencies: The benefits and challenges
pmc-13374526.creator: Stephen Jolles, Cecilia Poli, Nicholas L. Rider, Gabriela Negritu, Til Rendschmidt, Antonio Condino-Neto
pmc-13374526.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This review article considers the utility of calculated globulin as an unbiased and inexpensive screening tool for immunodeficiency. The benefits and practicalities of its clinical implementation and current challenges and limitations are discussed. Introduction

Primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs), also referred to as (part of) inborn errors of immunity (IEI), are a heterogenous group of disorders that affect ∼1 to 6 in 10,000 individuals (1, 2).

pmc-13663198.title: Can physical education be used to promote social justice? Conceptualizing a framework and thematic domains
pmc-13663198.creator: Corinne Lovett, Alex Filamor, Negin Fouladi, James Barry, Joshua Bernstein, Basil H Aboul-Enein
pmc-13663198.description: Social justice is a concept that is well-recognized yet difficult to define within the context of school curricula. As societies evolve and adapt, physical education (PE) curricula must reflect these changes. Student populations are becoming increasingly diverse, social justice issues and racism remain a public health issue, and the need to review existing school curriculum systems is warranted.
